content: US job openings unexpectedly rose in May to the highest level since November, largely fueled by leisure and hospitality, and layoffs declined, pointing to a stable labor market despite economic uncertainty.

title: ECB Wonders Whether Euro Rally Will Turn From Blessing to Curse
content: European Central Bank officials are starting to fret that a rapid appreciation of the euro could derail efforts to anchor inflation at 2%.

title: ECB’s Muller Sees No Need for Rate Cuts to Stimulate Economy Now
content: European Central Bank Governing Council member Madis Muller said the economy doesn’t currently justify interest rates that stimulate growth, allowing officials to take a pause from easing to gauge how activity withstands various threats.

title: Starmer’s Welfare Overhaul Hangs in Balance Ahead of Vote
content: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer is girding for what could be the most consequential vote of his premiership, with dozens of Labour rebels expecting to vote against the government’s welfare overhaul despite huge concessions to push it through parliament.

title: CEO Spends 1.83 Million Amex Points to Pay Surprise Tariff Bill
content: When a tariff bill for almost $11,000 arrived without warning, Robert Keeley reached for one of his last financial lifelines and cashed in 1.83 million American Express reward points to pay it.

title: UK Budget Watchdog Admits Optimism Bias in Blow to Reeves
content: Britain’s fiscal watchdog said it has been too optimistic about the country’s medium-term growth prospects and promised a full evaluation of the economy’s speed limit over the summer in what will be a crucial moment for Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves.

title: Citi Sees Zambian Kwacha Rally Extending If Copper-Price Link Restored
content: Zambia’s currency appears set for sustained gains if its correlation with the copper price is restored, Citigroup Inc said.

title: BOE’s Bailey Says Low UK Debt Making High Rates Less Effective
content: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said high interest rates are having less of an impact on inflation because of Britain’s low levels of debt among both businesses and consumers.

title: BOJ’s Ueda Still Needs More Information to Decide Next Rate Hike
content: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda ramped up his message that he is going to wait for additional data to make a judgment on the next monetary policy decision, signaling that he’s in no rush to raise borrowing costs.

title: Powell Reiterates Fed Would Have Cut More If Not for Tariffs
content: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell repeated that the US central bank probably would have cut rates further this year absent President Donald Trump’s expanded use of tariffs.

title: US Manufacturing Activity Contracted in June for a Fourth Month
content: US factory activity contracted in June for a fourth consecutive month as orders and employment shrank at a faster pace, extending the malaise in manufacturing.

title: BOK’s Rhee Says Tariff Impact on Growth Remains Policy Challenge
content: The Bank of Korea remains concerned at the tariff impact on economic expansion rather than inflation and is judging how to keep cutting interest rates while weighing stability risks, according to Governor Rhee Chang-yong.

title: EU to Accept Trump Universal Tariff But Seeks Key Exemptions
content: The European Union is willing to accept a trade arrangement with the US that includes a 10% universal tariff on many of the bloc’s exports, but wants the US to commit to lower rates than that on key sectors such as pharmaceuticals, alcohol, semiconductors and commercial aircraft.

title: Euro-Zone Inflation Ticks Higher to Match ECB’s 2% Target
content: Euro-area inflation settled at the European Central Bank’s target in June, strengthening arguments to press pause on a year-long campaign of interest-rate cuts.

title: Chile Economic Activity Slips, Boosting Case for Rate Cuts
content: Chile’s economic activity unexpectedly dropped in May on declines across several sectors, supporting the central bank’s outlook for renewed interest rate cuts over the coming quarters.

title: Iran Shuts Out Nuclear Monitors in Tactics Echoing Cold War
content: Iran is said to be cutting off communication with key United Nations watchdog officials, deepening uncertainty over the status of its nuclear program and introducing additional ambiguity to the diplomatic showdown with Washington.

title: Anna Paulson Takes Reins as President of Philadelphia Fed
content: Anna Paulson takes over Tuesday as the first female president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, after over two decades on the staff of the Chicago Fed.

title: Turkey Considers Raising Cap on Loan Growth in Early Easing Sign
content: Turkey is discussing loosening limits on some commercial loans, according to people familiar with the matter, signaling policymakers are comfortable starting to ease financing conditions.

title: Greggs Plunges After Warning Hot Weather May Dent Earnings
content: Greggs Plc shares plunged after it said its full-year profit may be lower than last year as high temperatures in June discouraged people from eating out.

title: Biggest Hedge Funds Extend Gains During Chaotic Six Months
content: The biggest hedge funds added to their gains in June, sailing through the first half of the year amid global market chaos sparked by President Donald Trump’s tariffs and the Israel-Iran war.

title: Santander Agrees to Buy Sabadell’s TSB Unit for £2.7 Billion
content: Banco Santander SA agreed to buy Banco Sabadell SA’s UK unit for £2.65 billion ($3.64 billion), a deal that will make it the UK’s third-largest lender by some measures.

title: Domino’s Australia Shares Sink as CEO Plans Exit After One Year
content: Shares of Domino’s Pizza Enterprises Ltd. tumbled to their lowest since 2014 after the company said Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director Mark van Dyck will step down after just one year in the role.

title: BYD’s June Car Sales Climb to New High After Major Discounts
content: BYD Co.’s sales climbed to a fresh monthly high for 2025 after a round of price cuts, though the move sparked scrutiny from government authorities and drew criticism from industry groups.

title: Hong Kong to Reclaim Top Spot in Global IPOs, PwC Says
content: Hong Kong is on track to regain its position as the world’s top fundraising venue for initial public offerings in 2025, according to consulting and accounting firm PwC.

title: Worldline Hires Auditor to Assess Risky Clients, Chairman Says
content: Worldline SA hired an external firm to go through its portfolio of risky clients as the payments firm seeks to restore trust following media allegations that it turned a blind eye to fraud pummeled its share price.

title: KKR Agrees to Buy Spectris for £4.1 Billion, Challenging Advent
content: KKR & Co. has agreed to buy Spectris Plc in a deal that values the UK maker of precision and testing equipment and software at about £4.1 billion ($5.6 billion), surpassing an earlier bid by a consortium led by Advent.

title: Paramount Settles Trump’s ‘60 Minutes’ Suit for $16 Million
content: Paramount Global reached a settlement with President Donald Trump over a lawsuit that alleged election interference by the company’s CBS news network when it showed two different versions of a 60 Minutes interview with then-Vice President Kamala Harris in October.

title: Manhattan Home Sales Surge 17% With Cash Buyers Leading the Way
content: Manhattan home sales in the second quarter were stronger than they’ve been in almost two years, boosted by cash buyers undeterred by the economic uncertainty created by President Donald Trump’s trade war.

title: Major Chinese Ports Keep Iranian Oil Flowing Despite Sanctions
content: Some of China’s largest ports have received Iranian crude this year, supporting a multi-billion oil trade and highlighting a significant gap in US efforts to curb funds for Tehran’s military and to uphold existing sanctions.

title: Qantas Says ‘Significant’ Cyberattack Targeted Flyers’ Data
content: Qantas Airways Ltd. expects that a “significant” amount of customer data was stolen by a cyberattack targeting one of its contact centers.

title: Canned-Food Producer Del Monte Foods Files for Bankruptcy
content: Canned fruit company Del Monte Foods filed for bankruptcy, less than a year after executing a controversial debt restructuring.

title: Goldman Names Maliah Global Chairman of Investment Banking
content: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. named Raghav Maliah global chairman of investment banking, in addition to his regional roles in Asia, according to an internal memo.

title: Biggest US Banks Boost Payouts After Lighter Fed Stress Test
content: Wall Street’s largest lenders boosted their dividends after passing this year’s Federal Reserve stress tests, a hurdle that regulators made easier to clear by softening some of the requirements laid out in previous years.

title: Hyundai Sharpens User Experience Focus With New Research Lab
content: Hyundai Motor Co. is deepening its push into understanding how drivers experience vehicles with the launch of a new showroom and research lab in Seoul, part of a broader effort to embed next-generation software into its cars.

title: India’s Biocon Aims to Lead Copycat Wegovy Sales in Canada From Next Year
content: Biocon Ltd. plans to file for regulatory approvals of generic versions of Novo Nordisk A/S’s Ozempic and Wegovy in key markets as it races to be among the first few to reap a windfall after patents on the blockbuster weight-loss drugs expire next year.

title: Stellantis Sales Drop 10% in Second Quarter Despite Ram Rebound
content: Stellantis NV’s US deliveries fell 10% in the second quarter even as sales of its key Jeep and Ram brands improved, showing the beleaguered automaker is making some progress in its slog to recapture lost share.

title: Sean Combs Jurors Say They’ve Reached Verdict on Four Counts
content: Jurors in the Sean “Diddy” Combs case were instructed to continue deliberating after they told the judge they’d reached a verdict on sex trafficking and prostitution charges but were divided on a lone racketeering charge.

title: Centene Plunges After Insurer Withdraws 2025 Guidance
content: Centene Corp. shares tumbled after the health insurer pulled its 2025 guidance, citing insurance market trends that veered from its assumptions and threaten $1.8 billion in revenue.

title: Constellation Earnings Falter on Softer Demand for Wine, Spirits
content: Constellation Brands Inc. profit trailed expectations in the first quarter due to weaker consumer demand for alcoholic beverages and higher costs from aluminum tariffs.

title: Bezos-Backed Satellite Conducting Climate Research Loses Power
content: An environmental nonprofit has lost communication with a methane-tracking satellite backed by billionaire Jeff Bezos.

title: Warner Music and Bain Set Venture, Seek Red Hot Chili Peppers Songs
content: Warner Music Group Corp. announced a $300 million cost-savings drive, part of an effort to free up funds for growth initiatives, including a just-announced joint venture to acquire music catalogs.

title: Toyota Delays EV Plans to Boost Gas-Fueled SUV Output
content: Toyota Motor Corp. is tapping the brakes on plans to build electric vehicles in the US to free up manufacturing capacity for a popular gas-powered SUV.

title: Bally’s Sells Interactive Casino Unit to Intralot in $3.2 Billion Deal
content: Bally’s Corp. is selling its interactive casino business to Intralot SA in a deal that values the business at €2.7 billion (US $3.2 billion).

title: Boeing Poised to Split Spirit Belfast Factories With Airbus
content: Boeing Co. is preparing to split control of a factory complex in Belfast, Ireland with arch-rival Airbus SE as Spirit AeroSystems Holdings Inc. struggles to line up a third-party buyer for some of the assets.

title: Private Lenders Pitch Debt Restructuring for Pallet Company
content: Private lenders have proposed a potential debt restructuring for 48Forty Solutions, less than a year after Summit Partners acquired a majority stake in the pallet management company, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

title: New ‘Squid Game’ Season Breaks Netflix Records
content: The third season of Netflix Inc.’s blockbuster series Squid Game racked up record viewership in its first three days, reinforcing the Korean survival drama’s status as a global cultural phenomenon.

title: RFK Jr. Vows Overhaul of Lawsuit-Sparing Vaccine Injury Program
content: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said he plans to make substantial changes to a federal program that compensates people who have serious side effects from vaccines and protects manufacturers from being sued.

title: Ghana to Seek India’s Backing for Vaccine Hub as Modi Visits
content: Ghana plans to ask India for support to develop a vaccine hub when Prime Minister Narendra Modi visits the West African nation this week.
